Getting started

Reach a reviewed plan first.

This path prepares the toolchain and inspects the target. It does not change cloud or Kubernetes resources until you choose an apply command.

Current scopeOCI OKE is implemented. Kubernetes 1.36.1 is exercised by the end to end pipeline.

1. Clone a tested release

Use an immutable release for a real installation. The example below uses the current tested release.

git clone --branch v2026.9.0 --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/pyahu/open-cluster-foundation.git
cd open-cluster-foundation

2. Install the pinned tools

mise trust
mise install
mise run doctor

The repository pins Terraform, kubectl, Helm, Helmfile, OCI CLI and every validation tool used in CI.

3. Prepare local input

Configure an OCI profile, then copy the two example variable files. The copies are ignored by Git.

cp terraform/oci/bootstrap-state/terraform.tfvars.example \
  terraform/oci/bootstrap-state/terraform.tfvars
cp terraform/oci/foundation/terraform.tfvars.example \
  terraform/oci/foundation/terraform.tfvars

Fill them with values from your tenancy. Keep credentials, OCIDs and customer names out of committed examples.

4. Review the Terraform plans

mise run oci:state:plan
mise run oci:cluster:plan

The state bucket must be applied before the cluster plan can use its generated backend. Follow the detailed OCI guides when you are ready for that step.

5. Inspect the Kubernetes target

After the OKE cluster exists and a dedicated kubeconfig has been generated:

mise run k8s:base:check
mise run k8s:base:render -- --environment starter

The preflight shows the current context, detected installation mode and selected profile. Read that output before applying the base.
